title: Dimension of the simple module at the first restricted rho weight
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $S$ be a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]: it is smooth, connected, affine and of finite type, has no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup, and every surjective homomorphism from a semisimple group with finite central kernel is an isomorphism. Solvable means that successive commutator subgroup schemes become trivial; finite central means finite-dimensional coordinate algebra and commuting after every scalar extension. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq S$ and a Borel subgroup $B\supseteq T$ with unipotent radical $U$, with these notions as in [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules]. Use the character lattice $X=X^*(T)$, roots $\Phi$, positive roots $\Phi^+$ in $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$, simple roots $\Delta$, coroots and integer pairing of [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. Put $\rho=\tfrac12\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\alpha\in X$ as in [lem-sfb-rho-section-modules]. A rational $S$-module is an $F$-vector space $V$ with coaction $c_V:V\to V\otimes_F F[S]$ satisfying coassociativity and the counit identity. A submodule is a linear subspace stable under this coaction, and simple means nonzero with only zero and itself as submodules. Write $V^U$ for the vectors whose restricted coaction is $v\mapsto v\otimes1$. A finite-dimensional simple module has highest weight $\eta\in X$ if $V^U$ is one-dimensional and $t v=\eta(t)v$ on this line after every commutative $F$-algebra extension. Write $\dim_F$ for ordinary vector-space dimension, an integer rather than its image in $F$. Assume $\operatorname{char}F=p>0$ and put $N=|\Phi^+|$. Every finite-dimensional simple rational $S$-module $V$ whose highest weight is $(p-1)\rho$ satisfies
$$\dim_F V=p^N.$$
This includes $p=2$, reducible root systems and the trivial group. No identification with an induced module is part of the assertion.

proof.text: Put $\eta=(p-1)\rho$. By [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure], $S$ is reductive with the stated root datum. By [lem-sfb-rho-regular-weyl-orbit], $\langle\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle=1$ for simple $\alpha$ and $w_0\rho=-\rho$. Thus $\eta$ is dominant and $w_0\eta=-\eta$. Let $E=E_B(-(p-1)\widetilde\rho)$, the actual regular-function module in [lem-sfb-induced-weyl-dimension-formula]. That node applies to $\eta$ and gives $\dim_F E=\prod_{\alpha>0}\langle p\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle/\langle\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle=p^N$. All fractions are in $\mathbf Q$; no division takes place in $F$.

proof.text: Since $w_0\eta=-\eta$, this same regular-function space with this same left action is $I(\eta)$ of [lem-sfb-induced-composition-linkage]. Choose its finite composition series. Exactly one factor has highest weight $\eta$; every other factor would have dominant highest weight $\mu<\eta$ with $\mu+\rho=w(\eta+\rho)+p\gamma=p(w\rho+\gamma)$, where $\gamma\in Q$.

proof.text: There are therefore no lower factors. The series from step 2 has exactly one factor, so $E$ itself is simple and has highest weight $\eta$. The given $V$ and $E$ are finite-dimensional simple rational modules of the same group and the same highest weight; [lem-sfb-simple-module-dual-highest-weight] gives an equivariant linear isomorphism. Transporting a basis along it gives $\dim_F V=\dim_F E=p^N$. For the trivial group the empty product is $1$, as required. The argument used only $p\ge2$ and integral weight pairings, so includes $p=2$.
